\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Memory-machine configuration guard]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.MGuard}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.MGuard}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MConf, Complexity.LogProg.Pre, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
Let $A$ be a memory-register program with $m$ registers and access to $d$ Boolean
deciders, let $O$ be such an oracle, and let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine with
$k_D$ work tapes. Given a state map $q_0$ for the deciders, natural-number bounds
$B,W,P$, an input bit string $x$, and a configuration $c$, the guard holds exactly when
the deterministic program obtained from $A$ by replacing every nondeterministic choice
with the answer $0$ satisfies the predicate $\mathrm{Pre}$ at bound $B$, input $x$, and
the control/register component of $c$; moreover, every register value $v$ satisfies
$|\mathrm{bits}(v+1)|\le W$, and the absolute value of the memory-head position is at
most $P$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation of a memory-augmented program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.marm_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.marm_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MBox, Complexity.LogProg.MGuard, Complexity.LogProg.MIns.isMem, Complexity.LogProg.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases, Complexity.LogProg.mbox_mseam, Complexity.LogProg.mcompileTM, Complexity.LogProg.mdet_halt, Complexity.LogProg.mdet_live, Complexity.LogProg.mmem_step, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_halted, Complexity.LogProg.mrun_succ, Complexity.LogProg.mseam, Complexity.LogProg.mstep, Complexity.LogProg.mstep_det, Complexity.LogProg.runFrom_forall_append, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{6}
Fix a bit string $x$, a memory-augmented register program $A$ with start label $l_0$, an
oracle, a Boolean multi-tape decider $D$ with initial states $q_0$, and natural-number
bounds $B,W,P$. Suppose that after $N$ steps, the run of $A$ from label $l$, register
values $v$, memory contents $M$, and memory-head position $p$ has halted with answer
$b$, and that every configuration at time $t<N$ satisfies the memory guard: its decider
calls meet the stated cleanliness and distinct-argument conditions, its register
encodings have bit-length at most $W$, and its memory head has absolute position at most
$P$. Then the compiled Turing machine, started from the corresponding configuration with
register values zero, memory contents $M$, head position $p$, and output word $out$,
halts after some number $T$ of steps with output $out$ followed by $b$, and throughout
those steps every register head lies between $-1$ and $W$, every decider-work-tape head
has absolute position at most $B$, and the memory head has absolute position at most
$P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Last Tape Cell After One Step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.step_last_cell}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.step_last_cell}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K$ be a natural number, let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $K+1$ work
tapes over the Boolean alphabet, and suppose that on every transition its last work tape
either leaves the scanned cell unchanged or writes $1$. For every input, configuration
$c$, and cell position $z\in\mathbb Z$, after one step the content of that cell on the
last work tape is either its previous content or $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Persistence of True Cells on the Last Tape]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.last_tape_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.last_tape_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.step_last_cell, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $K+1$ work tapes, and suppose that every
transition either leaves the cell scanned by the last work tape unchanged or writes true
there. Starting from the initial configuration on any input, every cell of the last work
tape is blank or contains true at every time. Moreover, once a cell contains true, it
continues to contain true at every later time.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration count bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.runFrom_count_eq}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.runFrom_count_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.last_tape_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_injOn, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.posCode_injOn, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visited_of_ne_none, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead}
\difficulty{7}
Let $K,B,P,T$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $M$ be a
deterministic machine with $K+1$ work tapes and a finite state set $S$. Suppose every
transition either leaves the last work tape's scanned cell unchanged or writes the
symbol $1$ there. If the run of $M$ from its initial configuration on $x$ is halted by
time $T$, and at every time $t\le T$ the first $K$ work-tape heads have absolute
positions at most $B$ while the last work-tape head has absolute position at most $P$,
then the configuration at time $(|S|+1)(|x|+2)3^{K(2B+1)}(2B+1)^K(2P+1)(2P+2)$ equals
the configuration at time $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[A combinatorial count bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.count_bound}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.count_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{6}
For natural numbers $q,n,K,W,cs,m,P$, let $L(r)=\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor+1$ for natural
$r>0$ and $L(0)=1$. Then
\[(q+1)(n+2)\,3^{K(2(W+1+cs\,L(2n+2+m(2W+2))+1)+1)}(2(W+1+cs\,L(2n+2+m(2W+2))+1)+1)^K(2P+1)(2P+2)\le 2^{(q+4+3K(2((cs+1)(m+3))+1))(W+L(n)+1)}(P+1)^2.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Time bound for memory register programs]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.marm_dtime}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.marm_dtime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.BankS, Complexity.LogProg.CSt, Complexity.LogProg.CleanSt, Complexity.LogProg.MARM, Complexity.LogProg.MARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.MGuard, Complexity.LogProg.MHalt, Complexity.LogProg.Ph, Complexity.LogProg.Pre, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.bankK, Complexity.LogProg.bankStart, Complexity.LogProg.bankTM, Complexity.LogProg.bank_cleanRun, Complexity.LogProg.callSegs, Complexity.LogProg.cleanRun_mono, Complexity.LogProg.count_bound, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs_le, Complexity.LogProg.liftAct, Complexity.LogProg.marm_run, Complexity.LogProg.mcompileFinTM, Complexity.LogProg.mcompileTM, Complexity.LogProg.mcompileTM_init, Complexity.LogProg.memAct, Complexity.LogProg.mop, Complexity.LogProg.mrun, Complexity.LogProg.runFrom_count_eq, Complexity.LogProg.vword, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt}
\difficulty{6}
Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a finite state set with decidable
equality, and let $L$ be a language of Boolean words. Let $A$ be a memory register
program with $m$ registers, $d$ oracle languages, and states in $\Lambda$, and fix an
initial state $l_0\in\Lambda$. Suppose each oracle language $A_j$ belongs to
$\mathrm{LOGSPACE}$ for every $j<d$, and let $W,P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume
that for every Boolean word $x$, the run of $A$ from state $l_0$, with all registers
zero, no result, blank memory and memory head at $0$, and with membership in $A_j$
supplied as oracle $j$, halts with the characteristic bit of $L$ at $x$. At every time
strictly before halting, assume the deterministic-part configuration satisfies the
program precondition, each register value $v$ has a binary representation of $v+1$ of
length at most $W(|x|)$, and the absolute memory-head position is at most $P(|x|)$. Then
there are a finite-state Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $C$ such that, for
every $x$, $M$ outputs the characteristic bit of $L$ at $x$ within
$2^{C(W(|x|)+\mathrm{logSpace}(|x|)+1)}(P(|x|)+1)^2$ steps.
\end{theorem}
